note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. You may use a calculator unless the instructor says otherwise. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a "float" in a salon's cash drawer?
options: The total amount of money the salon takes from clients in one whole day
The money staff are paid as wages at the end of the week
A set amount of change put in the till at the start of the day
A tip that a client leaves for the stylist after a service

questions.stem: Why must the float be counted before the salon opens?
options: To check it is the right amount before any sales are taken
To find out how many clients will come in that day
So the cashier can take some of it home for lunch
Because the bank must be told the amount by nine o'clock each day

questions.stem: Why does the float hold notes and coins of different values?
options: So the till looks full and busy when clients walk past it
So the cashier can give clients the right change
So the bank charges the salon less in fees
So staff can pay for their lunch from the till

questions.stem: Before opening, the cashier counts the float and finds it is J$500 short. What should she do?
options: Put in J$500 of her own money and say nothing to anyone
Take J$500 from the first client's payment to make up the float
Ignore it, as the amount will even out by the end of the day
Tell the supervisor and record the shortage before taking sales

questions.stem: A client's bill is J$3,750. She pays with a J$5,000 note. How much change should she get?
Why should you keep the client's note on the counter, not in the drawer, until she has her change?
options: So the note can dry out if it is damp from her purse
So that other clients can see how much she has paid
So that there is no argument about which note she gave you
So you can check later, at the end of the day, whether the note was real

questions.stem: What is the best way to give change to a client?
options: Count it back into her hand, starting from the amount of the bill
Drop it on the counter and turn to the next client at once
Give her the notes and keep the small coins as a tip for yourself
Put it in her bag for her without counting it out loud

questions.stem: A client has a wash and set for J$4,200 and buys a hair product for J$1,350. What is the total bill before tax?
Which is a sensible way to check that a banknote is real?
options: Smell the note to check that it smells like a new one
Ask the client to promise that the note is a real one
Look, feel and tilt it to check its security features
Fold the note in half several times to see if it tears

questions.stem: A client pays with a note that you think may be forged (fake). What should you do?
options: Shout loudly so that everyone in the salon knows the client is a thief
Stay polite and call the supervisor to follow the salon's policy
Accept it and pass it on to the next client as their change
Tear the note up in front of the client to teach a lesson

questions.stem: A client pays by debit card with chip and PIN. Who should key in the PIN?
options: The cashier, after the client tells her the number
The supervisor, who keeps a list of clients' PINs
Anyone, as long as the card is returned straight after
The client, with the keypad covered from other people

questions.stem: What does "contactless" (tap) payment mean?
options: The client taps the card or phone on the card machine to pay
The client pays without speaking to any member of staff
The client sends cash by post so there is no contact
The salon phones the client's bank and asks it to take the money

questions.stem: The card machine shows "DECLINED" for a client's card. What should you do?
options: Tell her loudly that her card has no money on it
Keep her card behind the counter and call the police straight away
Tell her quietly and ask if she has another way to pay
Try the card ten more times until it goes through

questions.stem: After a card payment is approved, what should you give the client?
options: The salon's copy of the slip to keep for her records
Her card and her copy of the payment slip or receipt
A photocopy of the front and back of her card
A note of her PIN number written on the receipt

questions.stem: Why must you never write down or keep a client's card number or PIN?
options: It could be used for fraud, and it breaks the client's privacy
The ink on the paper may fade and smudge before the end of the day
The supervisor already keeps a list of them
The bank charges a fee each time a number is written down

questions.stem: A client wants to pay with a gift voucher from the spa. What should you check first?
options: That the client bought the voucher herself with her own money
That the voucher is printed on thick, shiny card with gold edges
That the client has a loyalty card as well as the voucher
That the voucher is the salon's own, in date and not used before

questions.stem: A spa voucher is worth J$8,000. The client's treatments come to J$9,500. How much more must she pay?
A client books a bridal spa day for J$18,000. The spa asks for a 50% deposit. How much is the deposit?
A client says she has paid her bill by bank transfer from her phone. What should the cashier do before she leaves?
options: Check the payment has reached the salon's account
Take her word for it and mark the bill as paid straight away
Ask her to send the same amount again, just to be sure
Charge her card as well, in case the transfer does not go through

questions.stem: Which of these should a salon receipt show?
options: The client's home address, date of birth and her phone number
The stylist's wage and the salon's profit
The client's card PIN and the expiry date
The date, the items, the prices, any GCT and the total paid

questions.stem: How should GCT be worked out on a client's bill?
options: At any rate the cashier thinks is fair for that client
At the current rate set by law, as the till is set up
Only on bills that are paid in cash, never by card
Only when the client asks to be given a receipt

questions.stem: Why should the salon keep a copy or record of each receipt?
options: So the client can be charged again if she forgets to pay
So staff can find out which of the clients have the most money
So the day's takings and the accounts can be checked
So the salon always has spare paper for writing notes on

questions.stem: A pedicure costs J$4,000. Senior citizens get 20% off. How much does a senior citizen pay?
Who should agree to a discount that is not on the salon's price list or offers?
options: The client, who can choose her own price
Any member of staff who knows the client well or is related to her
The cleaner, who closes the salon at night
The manager or owner, following the salon's policy

questions.stem: A client is given a refund for a product she paid for by card. How is the refund usually made?
options: In cash from the till, always
As a cheque posted to her house
Back onto the same card she used to pay
As a voucher that she must use the same day

questions.stem: Before a refund is given, what should normally be checked?
options: The receipt, the item and the salon's refund policy
How much money the client earns each month at her job in town
Whether the client is a friend of the owner
The weather, in case the product was spoiled by rain

questions.stem: Why must a refund be recorded and signed off by a supervisor?
options: So that the client has to wait a long time before she gets her money
To prevent mistakes and fraud, and keep the takings correct
So the supervisor can keep the refund as a fee
Because refunds are against the law in Jamaica

questions.stem: Why should the cash drawer be closed after every sale?
options: To make the till print the next client's bill
Because an open drawer uses more electricity
So the float stays cool in the hot weather
To keep the money safe from theft and mistakes

questions.stem: The cashier needs to leave the reception desk for a few minutes. What should she do about the till?
options: Lock it or log out, and take the key with her
Leave it open so a co-worker can give change
Put a sign on it saying "Back soon" and leave it
Ask a waiting client to watch it for her

questions.stem: Why should large amounts of cash be taken out of the till during a busy day, as the salon's policy says?
options: So the cashier can use the extra cash to go shopping
So clients cannot pay in cash later in the day
To keep less cash at risk if there is a robbery or theft
To make the cash drawer lighter so it is easier to carry home at night

questions.stem: How should the salon's cash be taken to the bank?
options: By the same person, at the same time every day, so it is routine
At different times and by different routes, as the owner plans
In a clear plastic bag so it is easy to count
By a client who is going that way anyway

questions.stem: What is a "cash-up" (balancing the till)?
options: Adding more notes and coins to the till when it runs low on change
Paying out all the staff tips in cash at the end of the week
Taking all the money home overnight to keep it safe
Counting the takings and checking them against the sales record

questions.stem: The float was J$10,000. Cash sales for the day were J$38,500. How much cash should be in the drawer?
At cash-up, the drawer holds J$300 less than the sales record says it should. What is this called?
options: A surplus (the till is over)
A float for the next day
A shortage (the till is short)
A deposit paid in advance

questions.stem: The till is J$300 short at cash-up. What should the cashier do?
options: Take J$300 from the tip jar to make up the amount
Count again, check receipts and card slips, then report it
Change the figures in the sales record so they match the cash
Say nothing and hope that tomorrow it will be over

questions.stem: At the end of the day, why are the card machine's total and the card slips checked against the sales record?
options: To find out the clients' card numbers for next time
To see which bank each client uses
To check that the card machine is still plugged in
To make sure every card payment matches a sale

questions.stem: What does a till's end-of-day report (on many tills, the "Z reading") show?
options: The total sales for the day, by type of payment
The names and numbers of all clients who did not turn up
The amount of stock left on the shelves
The hours each member of staff worked

questions.stem: Why must payment records be kept neat, correct and safe?
options: So that clients waiting at reception can read them for interest
So the salon can throw them away after one day
They are needed for the accounts and tax, and are private
Because records look nice on the reception desk

questions.stem: A co-worker asks you to ring up her friend's hair service for less than the price list. What should you do?
options: Do it, because it is only a small amount
Refuse politely, and tell the supervisor if it happens again
Charge the friend the full price but give back the difference in cash
Do it, but only when the owner is not in the salon

questions.stem: There is a queue of clients at the till. What should the cashier do?
options: Rush and skip counting the change so the queue moves faster
Serve her own friends in the queue first, then the others
Close the till and go on her break until the queue is gone
Acknowledge the waiting clients and serve each one in turn

questions.stem: A client says she was charged twice for the same nail service. What should you do first?
options: Listen, apologise and check the bill with the sales record
Tell her she must be wrong because the till never makes mistakes
Give her cash back at once without checking anything
Ask her to come back next week when the owner is in the salon

questions.stem: A client has a manicure (J$2,500) and a pedicure (J$3,500), and buys a cuticle oil (J$1,200). What is the total before tax?
A client adds a J$500 tip for her therapist to a card payment. What should the cashier do?
options: Keep it for herself, since she was the one who took the payment
Record it as a tip, as the salon's policy says
Add it to the salon's own sales as if it were a service
Refuse it, as tips can never be given by card

questions.stem: Before opening, what else should the cashier check at the payment point as well as the float?
options: That the music in the salon is playing loud enough for all to hear
That every client has paid a deposit for the day
That the till is set to give a discount to all clients
That the card machine works and there are receipt rolls and pens

questions.stem: A client wants to pay part of her J$6,000 bill in cash and the rest by card. What should the cashier do?
options: Take both, and record each amount on the bill
Refuse, because a bill can only be paid in one way
Put the full J$6,000 on the card and give her cash back
Take the cash only and let her owe the rest until next time

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. You may use a calculator unless the instructor says otherwise. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A client's bill is J$2,850. She pays with J$3,000. How much change should she get, in J$?
What do the letters PIN stand for, on a bank card?
A card machine is often called a POS machine. What do the letters POS stand for?
A facial costs J$6,000. The client gets 10% off. How much does she pay, in J$?
A bridal hair booking costs J$7,500. The client paid a J$2,000 deposit. How much is left to pay, in J$?
What is the name of the form filled in when the salon pays its cash into the bank?
What word, starting with the letter C, is used for a fake banknote made to look real?
Which bank issues Jamaica's notes and coins?
Three clients pay in cash: J$4,500, J$2,750 and J$6,000. What is the total, in J$?
At cash-up, the till should hold J$62,000 but holds J$61,500. By how much is it short, in J$?
What one word is used for all the money a salon takes in sales in a day?
What do we call an app or account on a phone that holds money and can be used to pay, without cash or a card?
A J$10,000 float has J$5,000 in J$1,000 notes and the rest in J$500 notes. How many J$500 notes are there?
What is the small gold or silver square on a bank card that holds its data, and goes into the card machine?
What is the small amount of cash kept for everyday buys, such as milk for clients' tea or cleaning cloths, called?

essays.stem: Describe how a cashier prepares the till and the payment point at the start of the day in a salon or spa.
essays.modelAnswer: The cashier collects the float from the safe, as the owner's procedure says. She counts it with a supervisor or a second person watching, sorting the notes and coins by value, and writes the amount on the float sheet. Both people sign it. If the float is short or over, she tells the supervisor before any sales are taken. She puts the float in the drawer, in the right sections, and closes it. Then she checks that the till and the card machine switch on and work, that the card machine is connected, and that there are spare receipt rolls, pens, a calculator, the price list, the appointment list and blank gift vouchers. She makes sure the counter is tidy and that the cash drawer cannot be seen or reached by clients.
markingPoints: Counts the float with a witness and records and signs the amount
Reports any shortage or overage before sales begin
Places the float in the drawer by value and keeps it closed
Checks the till and card machine work, with rolls, pens and price list ready
Keeps the payment point tidy and the cash out of clients' reach

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how to take a cash payment and give change correctly.
essays.modelAnswer: First I tell the client the total, read from the till or the bill, so she knows what to pay. When she hands me the money, I say the amount out loud, for example "From five thousand", and check the note's security features. I leave her note on the counter, not in the drawer, until she has her change. I key the amount into the till, and it shows the change. I take out the change and count it back into her hand, starting from the bill: for a J$2,600 bill paid with J$5,000, I give J$400 and say "three thousand", then J$2,000 and say "five thousand", so she sees the change is J$2,400. Then I put her note in the drawer, close the drawer at once, and give her a receipt. Finally I thank her.
markingPoints: Tells the client the total clearly
Says the amount given out loud and checks the note
Keeps the note on the counter until the change is given
Counts the change back into the client's hand from the amount of the bill
Puts the note away, closes the drawer at once and gives a receipt

essays.stem: Explain how to take a card payment safely, and what to do if the card is declined.
essays.modelAnswer: I key the total into the card machine and show the client the amount so she can check it. The client keeps hold of her card: she taps it, or puts it in the machine herself. If a PIN is needed, she keys it in herself, and I look away and let her cover the keypad. I never ask for or write down the PIN or the card number. I wait for the machine to show that the payment is approved, then give the client her card and her copy of the slip, and keep the salon's copy safely with the day's records. If the machine shows "declined", I tell her quietly so others cannot hear, and do not suggest she has no money. I may try once more in case of a line fault, and then politely ask if she has another way to pay. If there is still a problem, I call the supervisor.
markingPoints: Shows the client the amount to check before payment
Client keeps her card and keys in her own PIN in private
Never asks for or records the PIN or card number
Waits for approval, returns the card and gives the client's copy, keeps the salon's copy
Handles a declined card quietly and politely and offers another way to pay

essays.stem: Explain how a cashier checks banknotes, and what she should do if she thinks a note is forged.
essays.modelAnswer: A cashier checks each larger note as she takes it. She looks at it: the colours and print should be clear and sharp, and the security features the Bank of Jamaica describes for that note should be there. She feels it: a real note has a feel the cashier gets to know, with raised print in places. She tilts it to see features that change as the light moves. She compares it with a note she knows is real if she is unsure. If she thinks a note is forged, she stays calm and polite and does not accuse the client, who may not know. She does not give it back to be passed on, or put it in the till. She calls the supervisor, who follows the salon's policy, which may include telling the police. She notes what happened.
markingPoints: Looks at the print, colours and security features
Feels the note and tilts it to check features
Compares it with a note she knows is real
Stays calm and polite, does not accuse, and does not put the note in the till
Calls the supervisor, follows the salon's policy and records what happened

essays.stem: Describe how a salon should deal with a client who asks for a refund for a product she bought.
essays.modelAnswer: I would greet the client politely, listen to the reason for the refund and apologise for the problem. I would ask for her receipt, or look up the sale in the salon's records, to check where and when it was bought. I would look at the product to see if it is faulty, damaged or not as described. Then I would check the salon's refund and exchange policy, and call the supervisor, who must agree to any refund. If it is agreed, the client can choose a replacement or a refund, as the policy allows. A card payment is refunded back onto the same card, and a cash payment in cash. I would fill in the refund record, with the date, item, amount, reason and the supervisor's signature, and give the client a receipt for the refund. The faulty product is kept aside for the supplier.
markingPoints: Listens politely and apologises
Checks the receipt or sales record and looks at the product
Follows the refund policy, with a supervisor agreeing
Refunds by the original method (card to the same card)
Records the refund with a signature, gives a receipt, keeps the faulty item aside

essays.stem: Describe how to cash up (balance) the till at the end of the day.
essays.modelAnswer: After the last client has paid, I print the till's end-of-day report, which shows the total sales and how much was paid by cash, card, voucher and other ways. I take the drawer to a safe place away from clients, ideally with a second person. First I take out the float for the next day, counted and bagged. Then I count the cash, sorting notes and coins by value, and write each amount on the cash-up sheet. I add up the card slips and check them against the card machine's total. I count the vouchers taken and any refunds or petty cash slips. Then I compare each total with the till report. If everything matches, the till balances. I fill in and sign the cash-up sheet, prepare the deposit slip and put the cash and records in the safe, as the owner's procedure says.
markingPoints: Prints the till's end-of-day report
Takes out and checks the float for the next day
Counts the cash by value and records it on the cash-up sheet
Checks card slips, vouchers, refunds and petty cash against the report
Signs the sheet, prepares the deposit and stores cash and records securely

essays.stem: At cash-up, the till is either short or over. Explain what the cashier should do, and why it matters even if the amount is small.
essays.modelAnswer: The cashier should not panic or try to hide the difference. First she counts the cash again, carefully, and checks her addition. Then she looks for the reason: a sale keyed in at the wrong price, a card payment keyed in as cash, wrong change given, a refund or petty cash slip that was not recorded, or a missing voucher. If she finds the mistake, she notes it. If she cannot find it, she writes the amount and the details on the cash-up sheet and reports it to the supervisor. She must never take money from the tip jar or her own purse to make it up, and never change the sales record. It matters because even small differences can show a problem with procedures, a till fault or theft. Honest reporting protects the cashier and keeps the salon's accounts correct.
markingPoints: Counts again and checks the addition
Looks for common causes: wrong keying, wrong change, unrecorded refunds or vouchers
Records the difference and reports it to the supervisor
Never makes it up from other money or changes the record
Explains that it shows problems or theft and protects the cashier and the accounts

essays.stem: Explain how salon staff keep cash and payment information safe during the working day.
essays.modelAnswer: The cash drawer is closed after every sale and locked, or the till logged out, whenever the cashier leaves the desk. Only staff who are allowed to use the till have the key or code, and they never share it. Cash is counted out of sight of clients. When the drawer holds a lot of cash, the extra is taken out, recorded and put in the safe, as the owner's policy says. Trips to the bank are made at different times and by different routes, ideally by two people. Card details and PINs are never written down or kept, and card slips are stored safely. The client's PIN is keyed in by the client in private. Receipts and records are kept in a locked place. If there is a robbery, staff must not resist: they hand over the money, stay calm and call the police on 119 afterwards.
markingPoints: Drawer kept closed and locked or logged out when the cashier leaves
Keys and codes not shared; cash counted out of sight
Extra cash taken to the safe; bank trips varied in time and route
Card details and PINs never recorded; records stored securely
In a robbery, staff do not resist and call the police afterwards

essays.stem: Describe how a salon or spa takes and records (a) a deposit for a booking and (b) a payment by gift voucher.
essays.modelAnswer: (a) A deposit is part of the price paid in advance to hold a booking, for example for a bridal party or a spa day. The receptionist explains the amount and the salon's cancellation policy before taking it. She takes the deposit by cash, card or transfer, gives a receipt and writes the amount and receipt number on the booking. On the day, the deposit is taken off the total, and the client pays the rest. (b) For a gift voucher, the cashier checks that it is the salon's own, has a number, is in date and has not been used before. She checks it against the voucher record, takes the value off the bill, and the client pays any extra. She marks the voucher as used, writes the date and the number in the voucher record, and keeps it with the day's takings for the cash-up.
markingPoints: Explains the deposit amount and the cancellation policy before taking it
Gives a receipt and records the deposit on the booking
Takes the deposit off the final bill
Checks the voucher is genuine, in date and unused against the record
Marks the voucher used, records it and keeps it with the takings

essays.stem: Explain how a cashier can give clients good service at the till while still following the salon's payment procedures.
essays.modelAnswer: The cashier greets each client with a smile and uses her name. If there is a queue, she tells the waiting clients she will be with them soon, and serves each in turn without rushing the checks. She reads the bill out clearly, so the client can see each service and product and its price, and explains any GCT, discount or deposit. She offers the payment methods the salon accepts. She counts change back carefully, gives a receipt every time, and keeps the PIN and card details private. If a client questions the bill, she listens, apologises and checks it with the record, and calls the supervisor if she cannot solve it. She does not give discounts or credit that the policy does not allow, but explains this politely. Clear, honest and friendly payment leaves the client happy to come back.
markingPoints: Greets the client and manages a queue politely
Explains the bill clearly, with GCT, discounts and deposits
Follows the procedures: change counted, receipt given, card details private
Deals with a query by listening, checking and calling the supervisor if needed
Keeps to the policy on discounts and credit and explains it politely

practical1.title: Run the till: open with a float and take a series of client payments
practical1.brief: As a group, set up the Centre's reception as the payment point of a salon and spa, and run it for a session. Use only the Centre's training money and a practice card machine, or printed card slips if there is no machine. First, two members count the float the assessor gives, with a third watching, and fill in and sign the float sheet. Then take turns: every member works as the cashier for at least three clients, while the others play the clients using payment cards from the assessor. The payments must include a cash payment that needs change, a card payment (one of which is declined), a gift voucher or deposit, a discount from the price list, and a split payment of cash and card. For each one, the cashier works out the bill in J$, adds GCT at the rate the assessor gives, takes the payment, counts the change back, writes or prints a receipt and fills in the sales record. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Photos show hands, money and paperwork, never real card numbers or faces. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Training money (notes and coins marked for training) and a cash drawer or tray
A practice card machine, or printed card slips
Payment cards from the assessor, each giving a client's services, products and how she will pay
Price list in J$, gift vouchers and a voucher record
Float sheet, receipt book and sales record sheet
photos: The float counted and sorted by value, with the signed float sheet
Each cashier counting change back into a client's hand (hands and money only)
A card payment on the practice machine, with the declined slip and the second payment
A gift voucher or deposit marked and recorded
Each member's receipts for their clients
The completed sales record at the end of the session
checklist: Counted the float correctly with a witness and recorded it
Worked out each bill correctly in J$, including any discount and the given GCT rate
Said the amount given out loud and kept the note on the counter until change was given
Counted the change back correctly into the client's hand
Took the card payment correctly, with the client keying in her own PIN, and handled the declined card politely
Checked and recorded the voucher, deposit or split payment correctly
Gave a correct receipt and filled in the sales record for every payment
Kept the drawer closed between sales and never left it open or unattended
safety: Use only the Centre's training money and practice slips; no real cards or real card numbers
Keep the drawer closed and the training money in the room at all times
Wash or sanitise hands after handling money
Sit or stand with a straight back at the till and keep cables tidy so no one trips

practical2.title: Cash up at the end of the day and prepare the bank deposit
practical2.brief: As a group, cash up a salon and spa till at the end of a busy day. The assessor gives you a cash drawer of training money, a till report for the day, a pile of receipt copies and card slips, vouchers taken, a refund slip, petty cash slips and a float sheet. Somewhere in the papers there is a mistake that makes the till short or over. Share the work so that every member does one part and checks another member's part: take out and check the float for the next day; count the notes by value; count the coins; add up the card slips and check them against the card total; check the vouchers, refund and petty cash. Together, fill in the cash-up sheet and compare it with the till report. Find the mistake, show how it happened, and write a short report to the supervisor. Finally, fill in a bank deposit slip for the cash to be banked, bag the float, and put everything in the place the assessor names as the safe. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A cash drawer of training money set up by the assessor
The day's till report, receipt copies and card slips
Vouchers, a refund slip and petty cash slips
Blank cash-up sheets, bank deposit slips and a report form
Cash bags, a calculator and pens
photos: The float for the next day, counted and bagged with its sheet
The notes and coins sorted and counted by value
The card slips added up beside the card total
The vouchers, refund and petty cash slips checked
The completed cash-up sheet beside the till report
The report to the supervisor explaining the shortage or overage
The completed bank deposit slip with the bagged cash
checklist: Took out the correct float and recorded it
Counted their share of the cash accurately and recorded it by value
Checked another member's count and agreed the total
Checked card slips, vouchers, refund and petty cash against the till report
Found the cause of the shortage or overage, or followed the steps to look for it
Wrote or helped write a clear, honest report to the supervisor
Filled in the deposit slip correctly
Kept the cash and papers secure and out of sight throughout
safety: Use only the Centre's training money and papers
Count in a closed room or away from the public, with the door kept shut
Wash or sanitise hands after handling money
Keep the papers private: do not photograph or share any real names or numbers
